doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Freddie Green's solo, amplifier story and singing
summary: An anecdote about Freddie's amp being sabotaged, his scat at the start of 'Li'l Darling', and a tape of him singing 'Them There Eyes'.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I just read a story in this jazz anecdotes book about Freddie Green and that when Freddie got his first amplifier he wanted to do some soloing himself, and the guys in the band said that every time he went to solo, the rhythm section would like not happen because he wasn’t— so they would start sabotaging his amp every night. So he’d go to do a solo and he’d have to go back to this, and he finally just gave up. Now I don’t know if it’s true, but it’s a great—
Well he has one solo, I’ve forgotten what tune it’s on, which was a big joke — it’s one chord.

At the beginning of “L’il Darling” he goes [scats]. But we’ve got a record of Freddie singing, “Them There Eyes” I think it is. Yes, my cousin Andrew is a great jazz collector, and he sent Joe a tape of Freddie singing years ago. I can’t remember what the occasion was, but he was quite reasonable. It was sort of like a joke I think.
I think with Basie. Well not standing up in front of the band, but singing “Them There Eyes” with a band so I imagine it was Basie.
So he did do other things.
But he’s always been considered the rock of the band. And you’ve been through so many wonderful people in that band, haven’t you? © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
